title: An accelerator-based source of high-intensity quantum-entangled annihilation gamma photons
abstract: We present the concept and development of a novel accelerator-based source of high-intensity quantum-entangled 511 keV gamma-ray pairs produced through positron-electron annihilation. The source leverages the unique capabilities of the proposed Jefferson Lab positron facility to generate polarized, high-current positron beams with a well-defined time structure. These beams enable the production of entangled annihilation photons at intensities far exceeding those available from conventional radioactive sources. The resulting gamma-ray pairs can be characterized using Compton polarimetry techniques, providing a powerful platform for precision studies of quantum entanglement. The combination of high intensity, controllable polarization, and precise timing also opens new opportunities in medical imaging, materials science, quantum information science, and spintronics. Compared with traditional radioactive sources, the proposed system offers orders-of-magnitude higher photon flux, tunable beam parameters, and unprecedented control of the annihilation process. We discuss the source design, methods for entanglement characterization, potential applications, and future development directions.
summary: This paper proposes an accelerator-based source capable of generating extremely high fluxes of quantum-entangled 511 keV gamma photons via positron annihilation. By leveraging tunable beam parameters, the source allows for unprecedented characterization of entanglement using advanced Compton polarimetry techniques. This platform is crucial for fundamental physics research and validating next-generation quantum imaging concepts.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing a high-intensity, accelerator-based source of quantum-entangled 511 keV gamma-ray pairs to enable precision studies of entanglement beyond the limitations of conventional radioactive sources.
main_result: The proposed system offers orders-of-magnitude higher photon flux and tunable parameters compared to traditional sources, enabling systematic investigation of quantum correlations in high-energy photons.
method: Entanglement is characterized using Compton polarimetry techniques (single and double setups) applied to the annihilation gamma pairs generated by polarized positron beams.
model_or_system: The physical system is an accelerator source utilizing a proposed Jefferson Lab positron facility to generate highly controlled, high-current, polarized positron beams that undergo electron-positron annihilation into entangled 511 keV gamma photons.
key_observables: Entanglement Witness (R), polarization correlations between the two emitted photons, and coincidence selection performance in imaging applications.
important_parameters: Gamma Photon Energy: 511 keV; Beam Control: Polarization, intensity, and precise time structure (MHz repetition rates).
main_assumptions: The source is a high-intensity research platform for validating quantum effects; future medical PET devices will still rely on conventional radioactive isotopes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the source concept using positron beams, the setup for single Compton polarimetry, and the double Compton polarimeter used to measure polarization correlations. Tables detail expected beam parameters and entanglement witness values.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the need for a superior entangled photon source, details the accelerator-based design leveraging Jefferson Lab capabilities, describes the measurement techniques (Compton polarimetry), discusses potential applications in fundamental physics and imaging, and concludes with future development directions.
why_interesting: While focused on high-energy photons rather than typical AMO systems, the rigorous methodology for characterizing quantum correlations (entanglement witnesses) using controlled sources is highly relevant to open quantum system research and quantum optics.
